works/augustine-confessions/summary: Augustine's autobiographical prayer to God, narrating his restless search, his conversion in the garden at Milan (386) and meditations on memory, time and creation.
works/augustine-confessions/significance: Its prayer "give what you command" provoked Pelagius; it became the model of Christian autobiography and of grace experienced as rescue.
works/augustine-enchiridion/title: Enchiridion on Faith, Hope and Love
works/augustine-enchiridion/summary: A short handbook of the faith organised around the Creed and the Lord’s Prayer, written for a layman named Laurentius.
works/augustine-enchiridion/significance: A compact summary of Augustine's mature theology of sin, grace and predestination.
works/augustine-on-nature-and-grace/titl: On Nature and Grace (De natura et gratia)
works/augustine-on-nature-and-grace/summ: Augustine's reply to Pelagius' lost treatise On Nature. He argues that human nature, created good, has been wounded by Adam's sin so that it cannot be healed or fulfil the law without the grace of Christ, which is not merely teaching or example but an inner healing power.
works/augustine-on-nature-and-grace/sign: The first full anti-Pelagian answer that names Pelagius directly; it fixed the Western framing of nature and grace for a millennium.
works/canons-of-orange/title: Canons of the Second Council of Orange
works/canons-of-orange/summary: Twenty-five canons and a conclusion, drawn largely from Augustine and Prosper of Aquitaine, affirming that even the beginning of faith is a gift of grace, while rejecting predestination to evil.
works/canons-of-orange/significance: Defined a moderate Augustinianism against "semi-Pelagianism"; confirmed by Pope Boniface II in 531, then largely forgotten until rediscovered in the 16th century.
works/edwards-sinners/title: Sinners in the Hands of an Angry God
works/edwards-sinners/summary: Sermon preached at Enfield, Connecticut, on 8 July 1741 on Deuteronomy 32:35, depicting the precariousness of the unconverted.
works/edwards-sinners/significance: The most famous sermon of the First Great Awakening and an emblem of the doctrine of eternal punishment in American memory.
works/gregory-nyssa-soul-resurrection/ti: On the Soul and the Resurrection
works/gregory-nyssa-soul-resurrection/su: A dialogue modelled on Plato's Phaedo between Gregory and his dying sister Macrina on death, resurrection and the purifying end of evil.
works/gregory-nyssa-soul-resurrection/si: Principal source for Gregory's hope of universal restoration.
works/julian-revelations/summary: Julian’s account and long meditation on sixteen "showings" received in May 1373, including the assurance that "all shall be well".
works/julian-revelations/significance: The first book in English known to be written by a woman; a touchstone for later hopeful eschatologies.
works/luther-bondage-of-the-will/title: The Bondage of the Will (De servo arbitrio)
works/luther-bondage-of-the-will/summary: Luther's reply to Erasmus' Diatribe on Free Will (1524), arguing that the fallen will is bound in matters of salvation and that God's foreknowledge and will are immutable.
works/luther-bondage-of-the-will/signifi: Luther considered it, with the Catechism, among his few books worth preserving; it marked the break between humanism and the Reformation.
works/luther-freedom-of-a-christian/titl: The Freedom of a Christian (De libertate christiana)
works/luther-freedom-of-a-christian/summ: Luther's short treatise, sent with a letter to Pope Leo X, arguing that faith alone justifies, unites the soul with Christ like a bride with a bridegroom (the 'joyful exchange'), and then freely overflows in love to the neighbour.
works/luther-freedom-of-a-christian/sign: The most widely read summary of Reformation soteriology; it holds forensic justification and union with Christ together.
works/palamas-triads/title: Triads in Defence of the Holy Hesychasts
works/palamas-triads/summary: Three sets of three treatises defending hesychast prayer against Barlaam of Calabria, arguing that the saints truly participate in God’s uncreated energies (as in the light of Tabor) while God’s essence remains imparticipable.
works/palamas-triads/significance: Source of the essence/energies distinction endorsed by the Constantinople councils of 1341-1351.
works/pelagius-letter-to-demetrias/summa: A spiritual letter to the young Roman aristocrat Demetrias on her taking the veil, urging her that God commands nothing impossible and that human nature, as created by God, is capable of holiness.
works/pelagius-letter-to-demetrias/signi: The most complete surviving statement of Pelagius' own teaching (long transmitted under the names of Jerome and Augustine).
works/smalcald-articles/summary: Articles drawn up by Luther for a proposed general council, distinguishing points that can and cannot be yielded; the "first and chief article" is justification through Christ.
works/smalcald-articles/significance: Part of the Lutheran Book of Concord (1580).
works/wesley-journal/summary: Wesley's published journal (1735-1790), including the Aldersgate entry of 24 May 1738 describing his assurance of forgiveness.
works/wesley-journal/significance: A primary source for the Evangelical Revival and for the Methodist doctrine of assurance.
works/wesley-plain-account/title: A Plain Account of Christian Perfection
works/wesley-plain-account/summary: Wesley's account of his teaching on Christian perfection (entire sanctification): love filling the heart and excluding sin, received by faith, often instantaneously, yet always growing.
works/wesley-plain-account/significance: Charter text of the Methodist and later Holiness doctrine of entire sanctification.
works/muratorian-fragment/summary: An 85-line fragment, discovered by L. A. Muratori in Milan (published 1740), listing books read in the church — four Gospels, Acts, thirteen Pauline letters, Jude, two (or three) letters of John, Wisdom of Solomon, Revelation and the Apocalypse of Peter (disputed) — and rejecting Marcionite and other writings.
works/muratorian-fragment/significance: Traditionally the oldest known list of New Testament books (late 2nd century, Rome); some scholars (Sundberg, Hahneman) argue for a 4th-century Eastern date.
works/athanasius-festal-letter-39/summar: Athanasius' Easter letter to the Egyptian churches listing the books of the Old and New Testaments, with others to be read by catechumens, and rejecting apocryphal writings used by heretics.
works/athanasius-festal-letter-39/signif: The first surviving list of exactly the 27 books of the New Testament.
works/tertullian-prescription-against-he: Argues that heretics have no right to use the Scriptures, which belong to the apostolic churches that received them; includes the question ‘What has Athens to do with Jerusalem?’.
Classic statement of the church's ownership of Scripture and apostolic tradition.
works/augustine-against-epistle-of-manic: Against the Epistle of Manichaeus called Fundamental
Augustine refutes the Manichaean foundational letter and explains what keeps him in the catholic Church.
Contains his often-cited remark on the authority of the Church in relation to the Gospel.
works/jerome-prologus-galeatus/title: Preface to the Books of Samuel and Kings (Prologus Galeatus)
works/jerome-prologus-galeatus/summary: Jerome's ‘helmeted preface’ to his translation from the Hebrew, listing the Hebrew canon and placing other books among the apocrypha.
works/jerome-prologus-galeatus/significa: Basis for later Protestant (and some Catholic) distinctions between canonical and deuterocanonical books.
works/vincent-commonitorium/summary: A guide to distinguishing catholic truth from heresy: Scripture interpreted by universal, ancient and consensual tradition; development as organic growth.
works/vincent-commonitorium/significance: The ‘Vincentian canon’, cited by Catholics, Orthodox and Anglicans alike.
works/luther-speech-at-worms/title: Speech at the Diet of Worms
works/luther-speech-at-worms/summary: Luther's reply before Emperor Charles V on 18 April 1521, refusing to recant unless convinced by Scripture and plain reason. The words ‘Here I stand’ appear in early printed versions but are not in the contemporary transcript.
works/luther-speech-at-worms/significanc: A symbolic founding moment of Protestant appeals to Scripture and conscience.
works/trent-decree-on-scripture/title: Council of Trent, Session IV: Decree concerning the Canonical Scriptures
works/trent-decree-on-scripture/summary: Lists the canonical books (including the deuterocanon), declares that truth and discipline are contained ‘in the written books and the unwritten traditions’ received with equal reverence, and declares the Vulgate authentic.
works/trent-decree-on-scripture/signific: Defined the Catholic canon and the Catholic position against sola scriptura.
works/westminster-confession/summary: The confession of the Westminster Assembly; chapter 1 ‘Of the Holy Scripture’ sets out the canon, inspiration, sufficiency, perspicuity and self-interpretation of Scripture.
works/westminster-confession/significanc: Standard of Presbyterian churches worldwide and, in modified forms, of Congregationalists and Particular Baptists.
works/wesley-sermons-preface/summary: Wesley's preface to his standard sermons, describing his aim to be ‘a man of one book’ and his method of reading Scripture.
works/wesley-sermons-preface/significanc: Key source for Wesley's view of Scripture and its relation to reason and experience.
works/pastor-aeternus/title: Pastor Aeternus (First Dogmatic Constitution on the Church of Christ)
works/pastor-aeternus/summary: Vatican I's constitution defining the primacy of jurisdiction of the Roman Pontiff and the infallibility of his ex cathedra definitions on faith and morals.
works/pastor-aeternus/significance: The definitive Catholic statement on papal authority; a major ecumenical obstacle.
works/hodge-warfield-inspiration/summary: An article in the Presbyterian Review defending plenary verbal inspiration and the inerrancy of the original autographs.
works/hodge-warfield-inspiration/signifi: The classic statement of the Princeton doctrine of inerrancy.
works/wellhausen-prolegomena/title: Prolegomena to the History of Israel
works/wellhausen-prolegomena/summary: Argues that the Law (Priestly source) is later than the Prophets and reconstructs the sources of the Pentateuch.
works/wellhausen-prolegomena/significanc: The landmark of Old Testament higher criticism.
works/dei-verbum/title: Dei Verbum (Dogmatic Constitution on Divine Revelation)
works/dei-verbum/summary: Teaches that Scripture and Tradition form one sacred deposit of the Word of God, that the Magisterium serves the Word, that Scripture teaches without error the truth God wanted put into writing for our salvation, and encourages biblical study and access to Scripture.
works/dei-verbum/significance: The modern Catholic charter on revelation and Scripture.
works/chicago-statement-inerrancy/title: The Chicago Statement on Biblical Inerrancy
works/chicago-statement-inerrancy/summar: Nineteen articles of affirmation and denial defining inerrancy, with an exposition; signed by nearly 300 evangelical leaders.
works/chicago-statement-inerrancy/signif: The standard definition of inerrancy in North American evangelicalism.
works/barth-church-dogmatics/summary: Barth's unfinished 13-part dogmatics (1932–67): the Word of God, the doctrine of God (including election in Christ), creation and reconciliation.
works/barth-church-dogmatics/significanc: The most influential Protestant theology of the 20th century.
works/tertullian-to-his-wife/summary: Two books advising Tertullian’s wife not to remarry after his death, or at least to marry only a Christian.
works/tertullian-to-his-wife/significanc: Contains an early eloquent description of Christian marriage blessed by the church.
works/augustine-good-of-marriage/title: On the Good of Marriage (De bono coniugali)
works/augustine-good-of-marriage/summary: Augustine defends marriage against those who disparaged it, naming its goods as offspring, fidelity and the sacramental bond.
works/augustine-good-of-marriage/signifi: Foundation of Western marriage theology for a millennium.
works/jerome-against-jovinian/summary: Polemic against the monk Jovinian, who denied that virginity was superior to marriage.
works/jerome-against-jovinian/significan: Classic, and in its day controversial, exaltation of virginity over marriage.
works/athenagoras-plea/summary: Apology refuting charges against Christians and describing their morality.
works/athenagoras-plea/significance: Early witness to Christian opposition to abortion and infant exposure.
works/luther-estate-of-marriage/summary: Luther praises marriage as God’s ordinance, attacks the canon-law impediments and celibacy vows, and allows divorce for adultery, impotence and desertion.
works/luther-estate-of-marriage/signific: Manifesto of the Protestant re-evaluation of marriage.
works/humanae-vitae/summary: Encyclical on the regulation of birth.
works/humanae-vitae/significance: Defining modern Catholic statement on contraception.
works/fiducia-supplicans/summary: Declaration on the pastoral meaning of blessings.
works/fiducia-supplicans/significance: Permitted non-liturgical blessings of couples in irregular situations.
works/evagrius-chapters-on-prayer/summar: 153 short chapters on pure, imageless prayer, transmitted under the name of Nilus and included in the Philokalia.
works/evagrius-chapters-on-prayer/signif: Foundational text of Eastern and Western contemplative prayer.
works/cassian-conferences/summary: Twenty-four conversations with Egyptian abbas on the monastic life, purity of heart and unceasing prayer (including the formula "O God, come to my assistance").
works/cassian-conferences/significance: Carried desert spirituality to the West; Benedict prescribed it for reading.
